mappings.note: Definition of a law as a described repeated pattern - the 'describing a repeated pattern' clause of LO-4.
Explicitly asks for the law-versus-theory difference in how each handles patterns - the describe-versus-explain edge of LO-4.
Asks for an instance of the third category, a principle giving broad guidance - the 'offering broad guidance' clause of LO-4, not the pattern or explanation clauses its siblings test.

Turns on 'theory' meaning something narrower in science than in everyday speech - LO-6 - with LO-4 supplying what the scientific sense actually is. LO-6 leads because the stem names the everyday contrast.
The stated strength is that matching observations build confidence in the underlying ideas - LO-8's first clause. Not LO-7: no particular prediction or its reasoning is asked for.
Tiny initial differences growing over time in a complex system - LO-10. Its neighbours on failed predictions sit on LO-8; here nothing has failed, uncertainty simply grows.

Directly about what happens when a prediction misses the measurement - re-examination rather than dismissal, LO-8. Kept off LO-5 because the trigger named is a mismatched prediction, not the standing revisability of theory.

Disproving the claim by asking whether any measurable mechanism exists - LO-6. The mapping stays on LO-6 rather than C5.2-LO-4 because the stem asks about the questioning method, not about where scientific thinking applies.
An estimate used ahead of the exact calculation to check reasonableness and catch errors - the cross-check clause of LO-9.
Requires supplying the assumed value (about 2000-2500 kcal a day) and working from it - the 'assumed values' clause of LO-9, distinct from the siblings that only argue estimation's usefulness.
When rough estimation beats an exact answer - a judgement about reasonableness, LO-9. No prediction about a future outcome, so LO-7 stays out.
The branches as human-made organising constructs over a boundary-free natural world - the first clause of LO-3.
Climate change as the named real problem that cannot be handled inside one branch - the 'gives an example of a real problem' clause of LO-3.
Asks what each of two specific branches contributes to one object, so it tests LO-3 at the per-discipline level rather than the general claim its siblings state.
Explicitly about students who leave science - scientific thinking applied outside science, LO-4 exactly. Not LO-3, which concerns branches within science.
Science as a human activity shaped by collaboration across cultures rather than a fact list - LO-5. LO-4 would need a non-science domain, which this item does not name.
Biology's version of the same simplification move: ignore the cells, treat the heart as one pumping system - LO-7's ignore-and-why clause, in a domain other than physics.

Marginal fit. The concept tag is collective growth (LO-5) but the sanctioned answer credits careful experiments rather than shared effort, so no outcome matches cleanly; LO-5 is the closest, as the question is about how science as an enterprise grows.
Learning from mistakes to refine understanding is LO-5 of C7.1; openly sharing results is the collective-effort clause of C5.2-LO-5. The item needs both halves.
Why models exist plus one worked example - LO-7's definition and its ignore-and-why clause. No competing question is offered, so LO-8 does not apply.

The whole comparison is theory-in-science against theory-as-guess, which is LO-6's everyday-versus-precise contrast, with LO-4 supplying what the scientific sense does. Same pair as the short-answer twin because they genuinely probe the same distinction.
Symbols and standard units plus the consequence of mixing unit systems - LO-6 across both halves of the question.

A vegetable seller's balance puts the SI standard (LO-6) squarely in commerce, so LO-4 - scientific convention operating outside science - is earned here in a way it is not for the laboratory-facing unit items.
Rebuts the claim that a theory is final - LO-5's revisability. Not LO-8: the prompt never mentions a prediction that missed.
A sustained comparison of the roles of law and theory - LO-4 at three-mark depth. Principle does not appear, so the item stays on the describe-versus-explain edge.
